policy: Real historical series only. Missing series are flagged and omitted from the chart, never interpolated or invented. Yahoo upgrades history is incomplete; empty is not proof of inactivity. Lead time is computed only from a documented dated entry (day or month-precision, labeled) to a real dated Street upgrade or earnings beat; modest same-rating target trims and already-constructive prior Street action do not create a lead. Month-precision placeholders are not exact entry days. COVID equity paths are not put P&L. Google Trends uses an explicit custom timeframe (not 'today 5-y'); values are relative 0–100 within that window.
event_study_method: Forward close-to-close returns from the first trading day on or after the documented date, using yfinance auto-adjusted closes, 21/63/126 trading days. These are market-path facts, not Camillo's personal P&L. Dates with only month precision use mid-month placeholders, labeled as such.
event_study_limitations: Sample is small and is drawn from stories he later discussed — survivorship and storytelling bias.
Several dates are month-precision; GME/AMC placeholders are mid-squeeze, which can flatten or reverse forward returns.
TPR uses the BI article date, which is a mention, not an entry.
RBI is a documented losing thesis; it is included so the study is not winners-only.
COVID positions were puts — equity-index forward returns are not put P&L.
Target × Missoni was an overnight options trade; the equity 1/3/6-month path is a different instrument.

pytrends 'today 5-y' from November 2026 does not reach 2019–2020, so we cannot honestly classify historical events into high-niche/low-Street quadrants. Wikipedia attention is a proxy only where the article exists.
Yahoo upgrades/downgrades history is incomplete. Zeros are not proof of inactivity.
No transaction costs, borrow fees, or options Greeks. Not a backtest of a tradable rule.
